: (I) design, (II) optimisation, and (III) simulation. The generative design capability allows both experienced and novice ship designers to rapidly explore efficient design concepts. The interactive feature is particularly tailored for the yacht industry, where designs must be not only high-performing but also visually appealing. In addition to design creation and optimisation, NeuralShipper™ enables users to develop machine learning-based surrogate models to bypass computationally expensive physical solvers for performance prediction. While surrogate modelling is not new, it has traditionally required strong machine-learning expertise. With NeuralShipper™, this process becomes straightforward, requiring only basic data and programming skills, making it easy for designers to get started. We currently have four users on board. Some specific projects of RSPL are outlined below. The Canadian High Arctic Ionospheric Network (CHAIN) was the original project of RSPL. Since 2008, CHAIN has collected GNSS and high frequency (HF) ionosonde data in order to measure and model the state of the ionosphere spanning polar, auroral, and sub-auroral regions. Currently, there is GNSS data being actively collected from 25 sites across the far north of Canada. CADI data is being collected from 8 sites, co-located with several of the GNSS sites. Unlike many other potential high-power EP systems, AF-MPD thrusters have a 60-year research and flight heritage and their technology is well understood, simple, reliable and robust. MPD thrusters have been previously limited by the large mass of the electrical components however, with the introduction of HTS, these obstacles can be overcome. The larger magnetic fields which can be generated with HTS enable an increase in thruster performance and an extension of the thruster lifetime. NSS is in close partnership with the institute of space systems (IRS) at the University of Stuttgart. IRS brings a long-lasting heritage of electric propulsion R&D development, in particular MPD thrusters, along with world-class facilities for the testing of high power EP systems. Human activity exerts spatially differentiated pressures on the Earth system at all scales. This includes ecosystem destruction, species extinction, resource extraction, pollutant emissions, soil sealing or waste disposal, among others.
